about.title: Personal Injury Help in Culver City, California
about.longDescription: Culver City sees its share of collisions along busy corridors like Washington Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and the stretch of I-405 running through town. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 80 injury collisions, with 113 people hurt and 1 traffic death — numbers that reflect how much local traffic funnels through these same streets every day, especially heading into the weekend rush on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, or in a fall, dog bite, or another type of accident, sorting out what comes next can feel overwhelming on top of dealing with pain, missed work, and medical bills. We offer a free case review and can evaluate the details of what happened. There's no cost to meet with us, and we work on a contingency fee basis — meaning no fee unless there's a recovery. You focus on healing; let our team look at your situation.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but if a government entity is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Missing a deadline can end your ability to recover anything.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of the fault.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages — like pain and suffering — in ordinary injury cases. That matters when an injury affects your daily life long after medical bills are paid.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed or pursued. Legal fees only apply if we recover compensation for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Culver City?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a city vehicle or public property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's important not to wait.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault system, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some responsibility for what happened. Your total recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't bar you from recovering entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Culver City?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes of reported crashes along corridors like Washington Boulevard, Sepulveda Boulevard, and I-405, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply counts from public records, not a judgment about any particular road or area.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free. We work on a contingency fee basis, which means any fees related to your case only apply if we recover compensation for you.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary personal injury cases in California, there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. This is different from some other states, and it can matter significantly depending on how an injury has affected your daily life.
